input.question: What are the contemporary general feelings / official teachings in Japan regarding their involvement in WWII?
input.ground_truth: I went to the Hiroshima Museum a few years ago. The history there was a complete white-wash. Every act by Japan was an "incident". e.g. The incident at the Marco Polo bridge, the incident at Pearl Harbor brought the US into the war. Even the Rape of Nanking was completely glossed over.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: What are the contemporary general feelings / official teachings in Japan regarding their involvement in WWII?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a big family, and a long time ago, some of your family did things that hurt other people. Now, some people in your family feel really sad and sorry about what happened. They remember the bad things and want to make sure they don't happen again. Other people in your family just want to move on and talk about happy things now.

In Japan, some people remember that their country did some very bad things during a big fight called World War II. They feel really sad and sorry for the people who got hurt. The leaders of Japan now teach in school that it's important to remember what happened and to never do those bad things again.

But, some people in Japan also want to talk more about good things happening now and don't want to feel sad all the time. So, Japan tries to remember the past honestly, say sorry when needed, and make sure everyone works together to have a peaceful future.
